question: The growth of professional road cycling teams and televised Grand Tours has introduced significant sponsorship income into the sport. This was one of many factors which changed the status of cyclists post-World War II (1950-present). Evaluate what impact the changing status of cyclists has had on the sport of professional road cycling.
markScheme:
Positive impact (sub max = 2)
- Increased sponsorship income has allowed top cyclists to train full-time and access better equipment, raising the standard of the sport (1)
- Higher standard of performance increases the entertainment value/profile of the sport (1)
- Increase in earnings available makes cycling more appealing as a career, increasing the talent pool and further raising the standard (1)
Negative impact (sub max = 2)
- Financial reward moved cyclists away from amateur ideals towards a win-at-all-costs mentality, changing the values of the sport (1)
- Competing for large financial reward has increased instances of doping/cheating which has harmed the sport's reputation (1)
Accept any other appropriate evaluation of the impact that the changing status of cyclists has had on the sport of professional road cycling.
Max 3 marks.

question: State one positive effect that modern-day 'amateurism' has on sport. Give an example.

- Amateurism viewed positively/promoted, eg fair-play awards in rugby union/Olympic Ideal (1)
- Opens up high level sport to all, eg amateur club sides taking on professional opposition in a cup competition (1)
- Amateur sport can be a platform to professional sport, eg through scouting of talented juniors (1)
- Less pressure on performers/more enjoyment/less deviance/cheating, eg fair play/respect encouraged in grassroots netball (1)
Must state a positive effect and give an example for one mark.
Accept any other appropriate positive effect that modern-day 'amateurism' has in sport with a sporting example.
Max 1 mark.

question: A leading rugby league club recently signed a forward on a reported salary in excess of £10 000 per week. Evaluate the impact that wages associated with modern-day professionalism in rugby league has on the status and motivation of players.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - Knowledge of modern day growth in professionalism and motivation: modern day professionals are respected for their talent, have more time to train, experience celebrity status and are positive role models in society. Motivation can be intrinsic or extrinsic, with extrinsic being tangible or intangible.
AO2 - Application to the status of a professional rugby league player and their motivation: the status of the player influences their ability to become a role model/their responsibilities can increase; as status increases they may have more opportunity to access better facilities and coaching; players may gain sponsorship from status; more money is invested in the sport due to professionalism; professionals train full-time and use state of the art facilities and equipment; some players are intrinsically motivated by love of the game while others are extrinsically motivated by tangible rewards such as wages/trophies or intangible rewards such as praise from teammates and fans.
AO3 - Evaluation of the impact of high wages associated with professionalism on status and motivation: the increase in weekly wages could increase intrinsic motivation to train harder and play better, increasing future value and making for a more entertaining game; alternatively players may become overly reliant on extrinsic reward and lose intrinsic motivation, which could be detrimental to effort/values; some players may be content to remain on the fringes of a squad while still earning large salaries; players may lose loyalty to a club while chasing higher wages; a balance between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation is ideal but over-reliance on extrinsic reward could damage intrinsic motives; higher wages may distract a player's focus onto sponsorship/media commitments rather than training; some professionals use their status to support charitable work/positive change.
Accept any other appropriate evaluation around the impact of wages associated with modern-day professionalism in rugby league on the status and motivation of players.
Max 8 marks.

question: Post-World War II commercialisation has impacted on sport. Discuss the effects of commercialisation on golf.
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points up to a maximum of four marks.
Advantages (sub max 3 marks)
- Increases in funding that come with commercialisation have led to better facilities/technology, coaching and opportunities (1)
- Increased funding leading to increased prize funds/opportunities for players (1)
- Increased funding has led to increased TV coverage of golf, leading to increased media involvement, which can generate more income for the sport (1)
- Golf can become a commodity of business, supporting the endorsement of products, bringing increased sales and subsequently increased sponsorship (1)
- Supports and encourages professionalism, leading to a higher standard of play/higher skill levels which can increase spectator appeal (1)
- More opportunity for grass-roots development/participation (1)
- Golf may see alterations to competition formats to create more excitement, eg shorter formats (1)
Disadvantages (sub max 3 marks)
- Viewing times and tournament structure interrupted by media advertising which may not suit spectators (1)
- Rules of the game may change, losing traditional nature/formats may change (1)
- Increased usage of technology reduces the flow of the event, eg video review of rulings (1)
- Money involved means performers may develop a win-at-all-costs mentality which could damage the sport's reputation/increase risk of cheating (1)
- Pressure to keep performing, making players anxious/fatigued/play when injured (1)
Accept any other effects of commercialisation on golf.
Max 4 marks.

question:
The table below shows the winning times for the men's Olympic marathon from previous Games:
Year | Time completed (h:min:s)
1952 | 2:23:03
1964 | 2:12:11
1976 | 2:09:55
1988 | 2:10:32
2000 | 2:10:11
2012 | 2:08:01
2016 | 2:08:44
Consider how commercialisation and the improvement in technology for sports analytics have affected performance in the marathon at the Olympic Games. Use the data in the table to support your answer.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - Knowledge of commercialisation and technology for sports analytics: commercialisation is the selling of a product for profit; to reach as many people as possible, commercial enterprises rely on the media, and the link between media, commercialisation and sport is often referred to as the golden triangle. Sports analytics is the use of data to better understand performance, eg athlete performance data, biomechanical data, fitness data; technology allows objective, valid and reliable data to be collected for further analysis.
AO2 - Application to the marathon runner: commercialisation makes more money available through sponsorship deals, allowing runners to finance full-time training with the best coaches, sports nutritionists and sports psychologists. Sports analytics technology, eg GPS trackers and wearable sensors, allows data on pacing/gait/physiological load to be collected and analysed to identify weaknesses or areas for improvement.
AO3 - Analysis/evaluation of the impact of commercialisation and technology on marathon times: despite the anomaly in 1988 (where times increased slightly), the overall data trend shows an improvement, from 2:23:03 in 1952 to 2:08:01 in 2012, a significant improvement over time. The anomaly could be explained by factors such as course conditions or weather rather than a decline in athlete quality. This improvement could be due to additional training time afforded by increased funding from commercialisation, eg lottery/sponsorship funding allowing full-time training. Increased revenue has also funded the development of sports technology, eg improved shoe technology and biomechanical analysis of running gait, allowing weaknesses to be identified and corrected, improving times further.
Accept other appropriate considerations of how commercialisation and technology for sports analytics have affected performance in the marathon at the Olympic Games.
Max 8 marks.

question: Explain how the modern-day amateur differs from an amateur of the 19th century.
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points
- (Status) - 19th century amateurs had high status whereas modern-day amateurs tend to have lower status compared to professionals (1)
- (Level/Quality of play) - 19th century amateurs were the best players, whereas in modern sports where professionals exist, amateurs are often unable to compete at the same level (1)
- (Money/Pay) - 19th century amateurs had sufficient private income and so were not paid, whereas some modern-day amateurs receive sponsorship or appearance money (1)
- (Class) - 19th century amateurs were members of the middle/upper classes/gentleman amateurs, whereas modern-day amateurs can come from any socio-economic group (1)
- (Mixing) - 19th century amateurs avoided playing against the working classes, whereas in modern day there is no such divide (1)
- (Roles) - 19th century amateurs were controllers of sport/selected teams/formed NGBs (1)
Accept other relevant differences between the modern-day amateur and 19th century amateur.
Max 3 marks.

question: The graph below shows the number of worldwide registered female cricketers between 1985 and 2015, rising steadily from around 150 000 in 1985 to approximately 900 000 in 2015, with the rate of increase becoming steeper after 2005. Using your knowledge of the factors affecting the emergence of elite female performers, analyse the trend described and suggest reasons for the results shown.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - Knowledge of factors affecting the emergence of elite female performers: there has been an emergence of elite female performers in the late 20th/early 21st century; although media coverage is still less than for male sport it has increased, leading to more female role models; more opportunities to join clubs, eg female-only teams/sessions; initiatives such as Sport England campaigns have raised awareness; work has been done to deconstruct traditional gender stereotypes.
AO2 - Application to the trend described: the number of registered female cricketers rose substantially, from around 150 000 in 1985 to 900 000 in 2015, which could stem from increased equal opportunities; the steady rise with an increase in rate after 2005 could be facilitated by greater media coverage of the women's game, leading to more female role models.
AO3 - Analysis of the reasons for the trend shown: cricket has become more available and socially acceptable so more women are likely to start playing; media coverage of women's cricket, eg the Women's World Cup, has increased awareness; more female cricketers means more people have heard of leading players, which can inspire younger players; women encouraged to take up sport may encourage their own children to do the same; there are presumably more clubs to cater for the growth, offering more opportunities to play competitively; governing bodies are more likely to fund women's cricket as participation grows; as stereotypes and women's rights have improved, more cultures/countries have allowed women to play.
Accept any other relevant analytical point and suggestion for the trend described.
Max 8 marks.

question: A rugby league match is tied after full-time and goes to a golden-point decider. Two players respond differently when asked to take the match-deciding drop-goal attempt. One player agrees and the other refuses. Analyse why the two players might have responded differently. Refer to achievement motivation theory and commercialisation in your answer.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - knowledge: achievement motivation is the desire to succeed/fear of failure; level of achievement motivation depends on personality and the situation; personality can be Need to Achieve (nAch) or Need to Avoid Failure (nAf); the situation affects achievement motivation depending on probability of success and incentive value of success. Commercialisation is the process of attempting to gain money from sport, an aspect of which is sponsorship, where a company pays for products to be publicly displayed/advertised to increase sales.
AO2 - application: the player who agrees to take the kick appears to be nAch; their personality/perception of the situation is positive towards the probability of success; they respond positively to the challenge, the roughly 50/50 scenario and the incentive value of the situation. The player who refuses appears to be nAf; their personality/perception of the situation is negative towards the probability of success; they respond negatively to the challenge, the 50/50 scenario and the incentive value of the situation.
AO3 - analysis: the player who agrees may perceive the attempt as an appropriate challenge to their ability and be motivated to meet it; they acknowledge the potential to succeed/fail and conclude they have the ability to succeed; they value the evaluation that will result from being watched, welcoming feedback; they value the opportunity to achieve and the incentive value, eg to win the match/be the hero; other factors may affect their choice, eg extrinsic motivation from a prize/trophy, or intrinsic value; if successful they could be seen as a hero, potentially leading to sponsorship deals, increased publicity and profile, eg media appearances, moves to bigger clubs and increased commercial income. The player who refuses may be predominantly demotivated by the evaluation involved, not welcoming the likely negative feedback if the attempt fails; they may perceive the opposition/situation as too great a challenge, with failure more likely than success; they may perceive their own ability as ineffective in such situations; they may prefer better odds of success; other factors may affect their choice, eg carrying an injury, ineffective extrinsic motivation, or poor decisions earlier in the match; they might worry about a loss of income from sponsorship deals if they are perceived as a failure, or about being portrayed negatively in the media, which given the high profile nature of the sport could lead to further personal intrusion or being blamed for the result.
Accept any other relevant analytical point about why the two players may have responded differently. Answers must refer to achievement motivation and commercialisation.
Max 15 marks.
